findings.issue: 'Displeased' after a deliberate pause is aristocratic understatement — the speaker is minimising. ساخط is wrath/indignation and removes it. It also inverts the intensity gradient against its sibling row in the same namespace (EFAF98A64B173370BC9DC4BDBB56313F), where the stronger English word 'outraged' is rendered with the milder غاضبون: as translated, the Justiciars come out angrier than the peasants, which reverses the English.

The other half of the pair. 'Outraged' is the stronger of the two English words and should sit above the Justiciars' 'displeased'; غاضبون is plain anger and sits below ساخطون as currently rendered. Fix both rows together or neither.
